I added the `flagged` subcommand to `skills/planning/critic/scripts/critic_ledger.py`, and it behaves as specified in a quick manual test. I didn't add a test file, since the repo has no test setup.

I ran five inputs by hand:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| Valid array wrapped in a ```` ```json ```` fence | Array printed as JSON, exit 0 |
| A JSON object instead of an array | `FLAGGED_DECISIONS_PARSE_ERROR: expected a JSON array`, exit 1 |
| An item missing `why_flagged` | `FLAGGED_DECISIONS_PARSE_ERROR: item 0 needs 'decision' and 'why_flagged'`, exit 1 |
| Invalid JSON | `PARSE_ERROR: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`, exit 1 |
| Nonexistent file | `PARSE_ERROR: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'missing'`, exit 1 |

It reuses the script's existing fence-stripping and file-loading helpers, so unreadable files and invalid JSON fail the same way `validate` does. A new `validate_flagged` function does the shape check. I also added the usage line to the module docstring.
